..
Visible satellite imagery shows a departing weak trade-wind trough 
that mildly disrupted the dry background trade-wind regime today. 
Starting tonight, low-end (10%) isolated showers and light to gentle
east winds will return for the Marianas through Saturday, becoming 
20 percent PoPs until the latter half of the week. Forecaster 
confidence is extremely low regarding the timing, intensity, and 
track of Invest 92W (see Tropical Systems section below) as the 
different model groups disagree from each other. Therefore, PoPs 
were kept at 30 percent for the last few periods of the forecast. 
Whether or not this system impacts the Marianas will greatly depend 
on its evolution for the next several days. Invest 92W will continue 
to be monitored and communicated.

Marine...
Benign sea conditions will continue for the rest of the forecast
period. Buoy data indicates combined seas of 2 to 3 feet, and is
forecasted to increase a foot or two by early next week. A low risk
of rip currents along all reefs will persist through the weekend.

Tropical Systems...
This morning, a weak tropical disturbance, Joint Typhoon Warning 
Center's (JTWC) Invest 92W, is centered east-southeast of Majuro 
near 5.5N 175.8E. Invest 92W is currently rated sub-low, meaning it 
is not expected to develop into a significant tropical cyclone over 
the next couple of days. 92W is seen along the eastern portion of a 
Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) found over eastern Micronesia. Invest 
92W looks to slowly move west-northwest over the coming days, with 
little or no initial strengthening expected through the weekend. 
However, we will need to keep a close eye on Invest 92W as it tracks
slowly west-northwestward as long range trends indicate development.

Eastern Micronesia...
A weak tropical disturbance, Invest 92W, is evident east-southeast 
of Majuro. Mostly cloudy skies with isolated showers is currently
over Majuro, with scattered showers seen southeast of the atoll.
Partly cloudy skies with spotty showers prevail across Kosrae and 
Pohnpei.

A quiet dry pattern is expected to continue through the middle of
next week across Pohnpei and Kosrae. Model guidance shows very dry
conditions remaining over both locations through the middle of next
week. That being said, Invest 92W could easily change that. Latest
guidance on 92W shows the system moving west-northwest then turning
northwest early next week. However, a strong mid-latitude high
pressure ridge stretches from the Date Line across Luzon, Philippines
and into the Asian mainland. This ridge may well keep Invest 92W
tracking much farther south than model guidance suggests. Therefore,
POPs (Probability of Precipitation) may well increase over the coming
days for both Kosrae and Pohnpei. 

For Majuro, Invest 92W sits to the east-southeast of the atoll. An
earlier burst of showers and thunderstorms is waning, however,
convection is on the increase to the east and southeast of the atoll.
Therefore, maintained scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
for Majuro through tonight, with a brief drier pattern Saturday. By
Saturday evening, Invest 92W looks to be a bit closer to Majuro and
is expected to increase POPs across the region for the next several
days. Latest guidance shows POPs mostly between 30 and 40 percent, 
though this could change depending on the development of 92W. Heavy 
rainfall is not currently a concern, but if 92W strengthens sooner 
than expected this could also change. All locations should monitor 
upcoming forecasts for any possible changes for Invest 92W.

Seas and winds look to remain fairly benign over the next several
days, with mostly light and variable winds and seas of 3 to 5 feet
across the region.

Western Micronesia...
There is a surface trough cross Chuuk currently, but convection was 
been pretty sparse with it. With no other upstream surface features 
to help focus surface/moisture convergence, we can expect dry 
conditions to continue across all of Western Micronesia. 
Unfortunately, just a stray shower or two is expected to occur from 
time to time. Look for afternoon highs to continue peaking in the 
upper 80s, with a 90 here and there possible. Lows will be around 79.
For the Mariners, light to gentle winds and seas of 3 to 5 feet will
prevail.
